wins.text: Full-year revenues grew 16% to $53.5 billion; EPS grew 77% to $40.54; ROE improved over 500 bps to 12.7%, demonstrating strong operating leverage
Q4 Investment Banking fees of $2.1 billion rose 24% YoY; net underwriting revenues rose 51% to $595 million; IB backlog rose sequentially and remains robust
Record full-year Equities net revenues of $13.4 billion; combined FICC and Equities financing revenues rose 17% to a record $9.1 billion

AWM management and other fees surpassed $10 billion for the year (exceeding 2024 target), up 15% YoY in Q4 to a record $2.8 billion; AUS reached record $3.1 trillion with 28th consecutive quarter of long-term fee-based net inflows
Returned approximately $3 billion to shareholders in Q4 alone, including $2 billion in buybacks and $965 million in dividends; 2024 was a record year for capital return by Goldman Sachs

risks.text: Platform Solutions (Apple Card partnership) was a 75–100 bps drag on firm-wide ROE in 2024; contract runs to 2030 with uncertain exit timeline, and the business has not yet reached profitability
Incentive fees of $393 million for full year remain well below the $1 billion annual target; deployment of $72 billion in raised alts capital is constrained by subdued transaction volumes
Ongoing regulatory uncertainty across CCAR, Basel III endgame and G-SIB surcharge calibration; GS joined industry lawsuit against the Federal Reserve over stress-test transparency
Provision for credit losses of $351 million in Q4, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio; total loan portfolio at $196 billion, up YoY

Broad macro and geopolitical risks cited by CEO: immigration, trade, tax and energy policy uncertainty under new administration; rising rates (10-year yield trajectory) flagged as potential dealmaking headwind

guidance_items.detail: 2025 effective tax rate guided to approximately 20%, down from 22.4% in 2024
AWM management and other fees expected to grow high single digits annually over the next several years
Alternatives fundraising in 2025 expected to be consistent with recent years (~$70–72 billion range)
Platform Solutions targeted to reach pretax breakeven in 2025, reducing its ~75–100 bps ROE drag
Incentive fees expected to continue progressing toward $1 billion annual target in 2025, up from $393 million in 2024

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Specific timeline and mechanics of exiting the Apple Card / Platform Solutions drag (management was notably guarded on specifics)
Pace of deployment of raised alternatives capital and the resulting time-to-incentive-fee conversion
Potential for strategic M&A in alts or private wealth to accelerate growth (management had not proactively addressed inorganic options)
